## Natural history notes

A small grass-veneer moth characterized by narrow tan to straw-colored wings with darker brown bands, pale striping, and small eye-like markings that give it a belted or patterned appearance. In Florida, it is found in grassy open habitats such as prairies, lawns, roadsides, fields, dunes, marsh edges, and disturbed areas where grasses are common. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on grasses and other low vegetation, often living close to the ground in silken shelters or among grass blades.
